question: Where do AES/MEva/CLAP/MIR cross from tie to lose along a dense continuous tempo grid (0.10-2.00) and over pitch shifts, and is MEva monotone in tempo?

operator_instruction.text: Tempo dense continuous grid 0.1-2.0; tie band 0.95-1.05, lose band <=0.80 or >=1.25, middle transition no prediction; report tie->lose crossing per metric; delete the 'x0.1 PQ should not drop' expectation; 126 pairwise win/tie/lose m=0.10*S; keep pitch design.

launch_authorization.scope: Eval-only scoring of ~49,300 tempo/pitch-transformed clips (MAESTRO 150 + 126b piano MIDI + TTM 5 systems subsample); AES/MEva/CLAP on GPU, MIR on CPU; NVMe peak ~15 GB; wall time < 4h. No generation, no training.

completion_evidence.method: guest writes terminal with sha256 of the registered summary after --validate-only passes

fixed_protocol.judgment: delta=variant-clean (same clip); tie if |delta|<=m; m=0.10*S (126a current S; D2/D3 unchanged); pass=80%; cluster bootstrap REP=400; directed metrics judged for worse, PC ties only
fixed_protocol.report: per-metric tie_exit and lose_entry tempo (linear interpolation between adjacent grid points) with cluster-bootstrap CI
fixed_protocol.meva_monotonicity: Spearman rho over tempo 0.5..2.0 per clip, cluster-averaged, expected > 0 with CI excluding 0
fixed_protocol.deleted_expectation: old 'tempo 0.1 PQ should not drop' removed 2026-10-20

resume.note: per-excerpt stimulus rows and per-unit scoring are idempotent; rerun skips completed units

revision_history.note: Rewritten per user 2026-10-20 decisions: dense tempo grid, new bands/crossing report, action implemented, smoke passed (138 clips).
